description: Frozen concordance triples extracted from MIMIC-IV. Prompt records require event time before T and storetime before T where available; records without true entry time are flagged as proxies. Decision-spanning reference records are identified and reported in sensitivity analysis.

temporal_cut.availability_cut: storetime < T when available; event-time proxy otherwise

provenance.case_prompt: MIMIC-IV structured tables (before the decision point)
provenance.ai_generated: Generation-model output (produced in a separate step)

sampling.selected_stay_rule: earliest ICU stay per Demo subject
sampling.eligibility_note: 100 formatted triples are not 100 clinically scoreable cases; use evaluation_eligibility and per-action observability.

generation.input_visible_to_model: case_prompt.text only (constructed from records before the decision point)
generation.note: Model-generated recommendations are not expert labels.
generation.system_prompt: You are testing a clinical action generation interface on deidentified data. Use only the record before the decision point. Return JSON with key claims, containing every distinct, concise, prospective clinical action you would recommend for the next 24 hours (up to 10), most important first. Each claim must have text, action_type, and target. Choose action_type from ordered, administered, treatment_performed, therapy_continued, monitored, specimen_collected, procedure_performed, imaging_performed, assessment_performed, disposition. Do not imply a medication was administered based only on an order. Do not claim knowledge of what clinicians did after the decision point.

input_fix.description: Lab/chart rows whose text result was lost (blank or numeric code) restored from MIMIC; only the Laboratory and Vital signs prompt lines were re-rendered.
input_fix.known_limitation: Chart rows with no valuenum at all were dropped by the original extractor and are still absent.

claims.text: Continue invasive mechanical ventilation support with lung-protective settings and monitor ventilator parameters, given current spontaneous breathing trial/CPAP mode and ABG showing adequate oxygenation.
Monitor hemodynamics invasively (arterial line, PA catheter, CVP) and continue vasopressor support with phenylephrine drip for persistent hypotension (MAP 59-68 mmHg).
Recheck arterial blood gas and lactate to assess resolution of lactic acidosis (lactate trending down from 4.3 to 2.4 mmol/L) and metabolic status.
Monitor and manage analgesia/sedation via fentanyl PCA, targeting RASS 0 to -1, with frequent pain and sedation assessments.
Continue insulin infusion and monitor blood glucose closely (fingerstick glucose 85-140 mg/dL) to maintain glycemic control.
Replete electrolytes as needed, including magnesium (1.8 mg/dL) and potassium, and monitor serum levels given ongoing IV replacement.
Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit (Hgb 8.4-11.4 g/dL, Hct 25-30%) and assess need for transfusion, with serial CBC checks.
Perform daily assessment of readiness for extubation, including spontaneous breathing trial and neurologic status (GCS, RASS).
Continue VTE prophylaxis with subcutaneous heparin and monitor for bleeding, given coagulopathy (INR 1.3-1.5) and thrombocytopenia (platelets 115-139 K/uL).
Maintain ICU disposition with continued monitoring and supportive care, including stress ulcer prophylaxis and bowel regimen.

claims.text: Maintain lung-protective mechanical ventilation with low tidal volume and monitor plateau pressures and driving pressure.
Wean supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 92-96%, avoiding hyperoxia given PaO2 388 mmHg on FiO2 40%.
Continue temporary pacemaker with rate ~60 bpm and monitor for bradyarrhythmia or pacemaker malfunction.
Monitor arterial blood gases and respiratory rate closely during spontaneous breathing trial or ventilator weaning.
Continue insulin infusion with hourly glucose checks targeting 100-180 mg/dL.
Replete potassium given whole-blood potassium 3.4 mEq/L and continue monitoring serum potassium.
Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit for anemia (Hgb 10.2-10.4 g/dL) and transfuse if clinically indicated.
Perform daily sedation interruption and delirium screening (CAM-ICU) with goal RASS 0.
Provide VTE prophylaxis with mechanical and/or pharmacologic measures given immobility and critical illness.
Mobilize patient with physical therapy and maintain head-of-bed elevation to prevent complications.

claims.text: Initiate or continue continuous renal replacement therapy for severe acute kidney injury with creatinine 6.7-7.3 mg/dL, BUN 89-93 mg/dL, and metabolic acidosis.
Transfuse platelets for severe thrombocytopenia with platelet count 12-13 K/uL and active critical illness.
Continue mechanical ventilation with lung-protective settings and monitor oxygenation, given intubation, FiO2 70-80%, PEEP 8-10 cmH2O, and persistent hypoxemia.
Continue vasopressor support with norepinephrine infusion and monitor hemodynamics for shock with lactic acidosis (lactate 3-4.8 mmol/L).
Obtain repeat arterial blood gas to reassess severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.22-7.24, bicarbonate 11-15 mEq/L, base excess -11 to -14 mEq/L).
Replete potassium intravenously for hypokalemia with potassium 3.0 mEq/L.
Replete magnesium intravenously for hypomagnesemia with magnesium 1.9 mg/dL.
Monitor blood glucose closely and continue insulin therapy for hyperglycemia with glucose up to 315 mg/dL.
Obtain repeat complete blood count to monitor severe thrombocytopenia and leukocytosis (WBC up to 21.6 K/uL).
Perform daily assessment of sedation and delirium with CAM-ICU and Richmond-RAS, given positive CAM-ICU and fluctuating sedation.

claims.text: Evaluate urgently for dialysis initiation or urgent nephrology consultation given creatinine 15.2 mg/dL, BUN 108 mg/dL, potassium 6.3 mEq/L, bicarbonate 18 mEq/L, and phosphate 8.1 mg/dL in a patient with dialysis-dependent status.
Obtain a repeat basic metabolic panel and venous blood gas within 6 hours to reassess potassium, bicarbonate, and anion gap after initial fluid resuscitation.
Perform continuous cardiac monitoring for hyperkalemia-related arrhythmia given potassium 6.3 mEq/L.
Administer intravenous isotonic crystalloid for volume resuscitation and to lower the elevated anion gap, with reassessment of hemodynamic response.
Assess dialysis access and ultrafiltration plan with the renal replacement team, given ultrafiltrate output of 1000–1300 mL and dialysis patient status.
Monitor strict hourly intake and output, including ultrafiltrate volumes, to guide fluid and dialysis management.
Recheck serum potassium and glucose after acute management, and monitor for hypoglycemia or rebound hyperkalemia.
